name: Beechcraft 1900
summary: 19-seat twin-turboprop commuter derived from the King Air, now mostly a cargo and commuter workhorse with Alpine Air, Ameriflight and Alaska operators.

wings: 1900D has small winglets; 1900C has plain tips
engines: Two PT6A turboprops in long over-wing nacelles, with four-blade props
fuselage: Long, narrow commuter fuselage with many small windows
1900D has a taller, flat-topped stand-up cabin
Small horizontal 'stabilons' fins on the rear fuselage ahead of the tail
tail: Small vertical 'tailets' under the tailplane tips
Twin ventral strakes under the tail (1900D)

tellTales: Small auxiliary fins on the rear fuselage and under the tailplane
Low-wing twin turboprop with a T-tail and a long thin body
Long row of small cabin windows

confusedWith.howToTell: The 1900 is much longer with many small windows, stabilons and tailets; the King Air 350 is shorter with fewer windows and no auxiliary fins.
The 1900 has a T-tail and a much longer fuselage; the King Air 90 is a small cabin twin with a conventional low tail.
The 1900 has a low wing and is far smaller; the ATR has a high wing and main gear in fuselage blisters.
The Beech 99 is smaller and plainer, with a low conventional tail and no tail fins or stabilons; the 1900 has a T-tail with fins and a taller, bigger cabin.
The Metro has a sharply pointed nose, a more slender fuselage and a low tailplane; the 1900 has a T-tail and fins on the tail cone.
The Saab 340 is rounder with a low conventional tail and large engine nacelles slung from the wing; the 1900 is narrower with a T-tail and tail fins.
